metadata.note: The Hudson Tubes: the first rail tunnels under the Hudson River and still the only rapid-transit link between Manhattan and New Jersey. William Gibbs McAdoo's Hudson and Manhattan Railroad opened its first tube between Hoboken and 19th Street at midnight on 26 February 1908, reached the Hudson Terminal in Lower Manhattan in July 1909 and Newark on 26 November 1911. The company never recovered from the Depression and the loss of ferry traffic; the Port Authority took it over in September 1962 and rebranded it PATH. Its Lower Manhattan terminal, by then the World Trade Center station, was destroyed on 11 September 2001, and the two services that used it did not run again until a temporary station opened on 23 November 2003 — a real two-year gap in service, drawn here as a gap.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PATH_(rail_system) (H&M opening dates, the 1962 Port Authority takeover, the four service patterns, 13.8 mi system route length, and the 2001–2003 World Trade Center closure)

metadata.not_yet_sourced: Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh here is an estimate; no PATH or H&M timetable was consulted. The pre-1962 features draw today's alignment, including the World Trade Center station rather than the Hudson Terminal it replaced in 1971. Whether the H&M ran exactly these four service patterns throughout 1908–1962 has not been checked — the modern patterns have been carried back.
